topics.name: Services Offered
topics.short_desc: Hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, kidney transplant, clinical nephrology
questions: What services do you offer?
What medical treatments are available at SKTI?
Do you offer hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis?
Can I get a kidney transplant evaluation?
What nephrology services are provided?
topics.answer:
SPMC - Southern Philippines Kidney Transplant Institute (SKTI) provides comprehensive nephrology and renal replacement therapy:

1. Hemodialysis: Inpatient and outpatient acute and maintenance hemodialysis.
2. Peritoneal Dialysis: Continuous Ambulatory Peritoneal Dialysis (CAPD) training and clinical follow-up.
3. Kidney Transplantation: Pre-transplant donor and recipient medical evaluation, kidney transplant surgery, and long-term post-transplant monitoring.
4. Renal Intensive Care: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) and hemoperfusion for critically ill patients.
5. Clinical Nephrology Consultations: Comprehensive management of acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease (CKD), glomerulonephritis, and hypertensive kidney disease.

topics.name: Hours & Schedule
topics.short_desc: Outpatient clinic hours and 24/7 dialysis shifts
questions: What are your operating hours?
What time does the clinic open?
What are the dialysis shifts?
Is the hemodialysis center open on weekends or at night?
What is the consultation schedule?
topics.answer:
Operating Hours and Dialysis Shifts at SPMC SKTI:

• Nephrology Outpatient Clinic: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM (excluding official Philippine public holidays).
• Hemodialysis Unit: Operates 24/7 across scheduled shifts:
  - 1st Shift: 6:00 AM – 10:00 AM
  - 2nd Shift: 11:00 AM – 3:00 PM
  - 3rd Shift: 4:00 PM – 8:00 PM
  - 4th Shift / Emergency Night Shift: 9:00 PM onwards
• Emergency Renal Services: Available 24 hours daily through the SPMC Emergency Department.

topics.name: Requirements & Documents
topics.short_desc: Medical abstract, laboratory clearances, and PhilHealth documents
questions: What are the requirements for admission or dialysis?
What documents do I need to bring?
What papers are required for hemodialysis enrollment?
What laboratory tests are required before starting dialysis?
What are the requirements for kidney transplant evaluation?
topics.answer:
Requirements for Dialysis Admission and Nephrology Evaluation:

1. Medical Abstract / Clinical Summary signed by an accredited attending nephrologist.
2. Official Dialysis Prescription specifying target dry weight, dialyzer membrane, blood flow rate, and anticoagulant regimen.
3. Recent Laboratory Results (taken within 30 days):
   • Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count
   • Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN), Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Phosphorus
   • Hepatitis Profile: HBsAg, Anti-HCV, Anti-HBs
4. Valid Government-Issued ID of the patient and authorized relative/caregiver.
5. Updated PhilHealth Member Data Record (MDR) and signed PhilHealth Claim Signature Form.

topics.name: Fees & PhilHealth
questions: How much does hemodialysis cost?
Is dialysis covered by PhilHealth?
How many dialysis sessions does PhilHealth cover per year?
Are there free dialysis services or financial assistance?
What are the out-of-pocket costs?
topics.answer:
Fees and Financial Coverage at SPMC SKTI:

• PhilHealth Hemodialysis Benefit: Under PhilHealth Circular No. 2023-0014, eligible patients receive coverage for up to 156 hemodialysis sessions per calendar year. Standard package treatment has zero out-of-pocket co-payment in accredited government healthcare institutions like SPMC.
• Specialized Supplies & Medications: High-flux dialyzers, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (EPO), IV iron sucrose, and specialized medications outside the standard benefit package may incur separate charges.
• Financial Assistance: Qualified indigent patients may request medical assistance through the SPMC Malasakit Center and Medical Social Services (MSS) located on the Ground Floor Main Hall.
